class FakeObjectMapper extends ObjectMapper {
   private Map<String, JsonNode> nodeMap = new HashMap<>();
   private Map<String, IOException> exceptionMap = new HashMap<>();
   void whenReadTreeReturn(String json, JsonNode node) { nodeMap.put(json, node); }
   void whenReadTreeThrow(String json, IOException ex) { exceptionMap.put(json, ex); }
   @Override
   public JsonNode readTree(String content) throws IOException {
       if (exceptionMap.containsKey(content)) {
           throw exceptionMap.get(content);
       }
       if (nodeMap.containsKey(content)) {
           return nodeMap.get(content);
       }
       return super.readTree(content); // fallback
   }
}

Actually JsonSchemaFactory is not final; we can create subclass TestJsonSchemaFactory that extends JsonSchemaFactory and provides a public constructor that calls the private constructor via reflection? That's messy.

Simpler: Use reflection to instantiate JsonSchemaFactory, then use reflection to set its protected method? Can't override after creation.

But we can use Mockito's spy to stub protected method; without Mockito we could use a subclass via anonymous class overriding newJsonSchema, but we need to call the constructor of JsonSchemaFactory (which is private). However we can create subclass that uses the same private constructor via reflection? Not possible.

Alternative: Use reflection to set the private field jsonMapper to our FakeObjectMapper, and then use a custom subclass that extends JsonSchemaFactory but overrides newJsonSchema. We can instantiate subclass using default constructor? There's no public constructor. So we cannot instantiate subclass directly.

Thus perhaps we need to keep using Mockito for spying; but we can avoid Mockito by using a custom subclass that we instantiate via reflection using the private constructor, then set its newJsonSchema behavior via a proxy? Can't change method implementation.

Instead we can test exception handling only (which only depends on readTree). For success case, we could just verify that getSchema returns a non-null JsonSchema (real). But that may be heavy.

Thus we can rewrite testGetSchemaSuccess to not mock newJsonSchema but just call getSchema and verify result not null.
